paper_metadata.title: Functional and Structural Network Recovery after Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A 1-Year Longitudinal Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a prospective design with clear diagnostic criteria (EFNS guidelines) and well-matched controls. The recruitment source (emergency departments) and baseline characteristics are thoroughly described, minimizing selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The diagnosis of mTBI was given in accordance with the European Federation of Neurological Societies guidelines (Vos et al., 2012) using standardized criteria across the emergency departments of four hospitals in the German region of Switzerland.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the clinical guidelines and the specific healthcare settings used to identify the population.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 60 patients with mTBI and 58 healthy controls matched for gender, age, and education were prospectively recruited between February 2012 and March 2014.
items.reasoning: The recruitment period and matching strategy are explicitly stated.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: prospectively recruited between February 2012 and March 2014.
items.reasoning: Specific dates are provided.

items.reasoning: The setting (emergency departments) and geographic region are clear.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria comprised (1) a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 13–15 at hospital admission; (2) a normal cranial computed tomography (CT); (3) at least one of the following characteristics: loss of consciousness <30 min... Exclusion criteria were as follows: history of neurologic or psychiatric disease...
items.reasoning: Detailed clinical and demographic criteria are listed.

items.reasoning: 49 out of 51 eligible patients (96%) completed the 1-year follow-up.

risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study matched for age, gender, and education, and adjusted for brain volumes in correlations, the small sample size of the PCD subgroup (n=6) limits the ability to fully account for confounders in that specific analysis. Additionally, treatments received during the 1-year interval were not explicitly measured.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical analysis is robust (NBS, permutation testing), but the authors acknowledge that the brain-behavior correlations did not survive FDR correction, and the PCD subgroup analysis is underpowered. There is also a risk of bias from the 'selective interaction' approach which might miss non-acute changes.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Connectivity analyses were based on a 90-node whole-brain network... NBS is a validated non-parametric method
items.reasoning: The analytical pipeline is described in detail, including software and thresholds.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: We then analyzed group × time interaction using NBS selecting exclusively the subnetwork identified as significant from the differences observed between groups at Visit 1 (selective interaction).
items.reasoning: The strategy is logically derived from the acute findings, though the authors also include a whole-brain interaction to avoid bias.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: computed directly with NBS with the component extent option... 5,000 permutations per statistical test.
items.reasoning: Permutation-based testing is appropriate for high-dimensional connectivity data.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: After the FDR adjustment tested across 30 correlations... uncorrected significances did not survive the FDR correction
items.reasoning: The authors are transparent about the lack of significance after FDR correction, but they still emphasize the uncorrected results in the discussion.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Statistical Analysis and Presentation Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: The statistical analysis is appropriate for the design of the study, limiting potential for presentation of invalid or spurious results.
